doc.title: Jones Hank — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Teddie's move to New York and the return visit to Charleston
summary: Teddie, the ninth of ten children, was raised in New York by her older sister Beebe, and returned to South Carolina with Hank.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: How did you come to New York?
An older sister. She came first. I’m the ninth child in the family. She was the fifth one.

It was Beebe because the fifth was Beebe. Beebe, which is… When you see her, you think she was a member of an Indian child. That is the look that she had. I was her favorite when I was born. She was so little when she used to come and play. They let her carry me around when she was much older than I was. She was married so she came to New York. Then, she came back when I was over 10 years old. She asked my father if she could bring me back to New York with her. They know that she has always been like some my mother. She took the place of my mother because my mother had 10 children, so she took over. Anyone with any kind of help was glued to her. She brought me to New York and it was supposed to be a trial thing for a year or so but the years went by and I stayed with her and I grew up.

I have always felt like she is my mother. My mother never got there that much. She's to come sometime in the summer. I was 18 years old before I returned. She saw the progress of the things that had taken hold after they converted to a city. So, they had things pretty well organized. Later on, I returned to Lincoln with Hank. That was one he did the Festival in Charleston.
That was for the first time.
That was for the first time and that was a beautiful moment.

That was first time I had ever been to her home. I met some of her relatives that were still alive at the time. Met her aunt and the person who is the mayor at that time. We went to his home, right? Yes, he was the mayor at that time.
Yes, I know who you’re talking about.
